name: Scotch Game
description: 3.d4 opens the centre at once: quick development and free piece play.

lines.name: 4…Bc5

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Be3 defends the d4 knight against the c5 bishop.
notes.10: c3 holds d4 a second time.
notes.12: Bc4 develops to the active diagonal towards f7.

10.Nxc6: …Bxe3! fxe3 and …Qh4+: your pawns fall apart.

lines.summary: Defend d4 with Be3 and c3, then develop Bc4 and castle.

lines.name: 4…Bc5 7.Bc4 O-O

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Be3 defends the d4 knight against the c5 bishop.
notes.10: c3 holds d4 a second time.
notes.12: Bc4 develops to the active diagonal towards f7.
notes.14: O-O: White's position is solid; Nd2 or Nc2 comes next.
notes.16: Nxc6 Nxc6 and Bxc5 trades off Black's best bishop and doubles the c-pawns.

10.Nxc6: …Bxe3! fxe3 and …Qh4+: your pawns fall apart.

lines.summary: Castle short, then trade on c6 and c5: Black's pressure on d4 is gone.

lines.name: 4…Bc5 7…Ne5

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Be3 defends the d4 knight against the c5 bishop.
notes.10: c3 holds d4 a second time.
notes.12: Bc4 develops to the active diagonal towards f7.
notes.14: Be2 steps away from the knight; the e5 knight will be kicked by f4 later.

10.Nxc6: …Bxe3! fxe3 and …Qh4+: your pawns fall apart.

lines.summary: When the knight hits the c4 bishop, drop back to e2 and keep d4 safe.

lines.name: 4…Bc5 5…Bb6

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Be3 defends the d4 knight against the c5 bishop.
notes.10: Nc3 develops; the bishop on b6 has no targets.
notes.12: Qd2 connects the pieces and prepares O-O-O.

lines.summary: If the bishop retreats to b6, develop with Nc3 and Qd2, then castle long.

lines.name: 4…Nxd4

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Qxd4: the queen is strong in the centre and hard to chase.
notes.10: Nc3 develops; Bf4 or Be3 and O-O-O can follow.

lines.summary: After the knight trade, the white queen dominates the centre: develop around it.

lines.name: 5…Qf6

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Qxd4: the queen is strong in the centre and hard to chase.
notes.10: e5 gains space with tempo on the queen.

lines.summary: If Black offers a queen trade with …Qf6, push e5 with tempo (or keep queens with Qe3).

lines.name: 5…Qf6 6.e5 Qb6

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Qxd4: the queen is strong in the centre and hard to chase.
notes.10: e5 gains space with tempo on the queen.
notes.12: Qxb6 trades queens; after …axb6, Black's b-pawns are doubled.

lines.summary: When the queen goes to b6, trade queens: White keeps the space and Black gets doubled pawns.

lines.name: 5…Nf6

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Qxd4: the queen is strong in the centre and hard to chase.
notes.10: e5 kicks the knight; White's space advantage grows.

10.Bg5: …h6! kicks the bishop and Black gains time.

lines.summary: Against 5…Nf6, push e5 at once and chase the knight.

lines.name: 5…c5

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Qxd4: the queen is strong in the centre and hard to chase.
notes.10: Qe3 keeps the queen central and eyes e5.

lines.summary: When …c5 kicks the queen, step back to e3, d3 or c3; Black's d-pawn is now weak.

lines.name: 4…Nf6

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.10: Bd3 defends e4 calmly; White plans O-O and quick development.
notes.12: exd5 trades in the centre; Black is left with a weak c-pawn structure.

lines.summary: Trade on c6 to damage Black's pawns, then Bd3 and exd5 against …d5.

lines.name: 4…Nf6 6…d5

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.10: Bd3 defends e4 calmly; White plans O-O and quick development.
notes.12: exd5 trades in the centre; Black is left with a weak c-pawn structure.
notes.14: O-O: White aims at the isolated d5 pawn and the c-file.

lines.summary: After the central trade, castle and target Black's isolated d5 pawn.

lines.name: 4…Nf6 6…Bc5

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.10: Bd3 defends e4 calmly; White plans O-O and quick development.
notes.12: O-O: White is ready for e5 or Nc3.
notes.14: e5 kicks the f6 knight now that White's king is safe.

14.Bg5: …h6! asks the bishop, and Black's pieces get active.

lines.summary: Against …Bc5, castle, then kick the knight with e5.

lines.name: 4…Qf6

notes.4: d4 strikes the centre at once instead of slow Bc4 or Bb5 play.
notes.6: Nxd4 recaptures with a strong central knight.
notes.8: Be3 develops and protects the d4 knight.

lines.summary: Against the early queen, defend d4 with Be3 and keep developing.
